You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: s3a-vectored-iostats
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/s3a-vectored-iostats.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/s3a-vectored-iostats.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: s3a-vectored-iostats" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/s3a-vectored-iostats.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/s3a-vectored-iostats.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"s3a-vectored-iostats","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators using S3A vectored reads need the same visibility into performance and waste that they already have for ordinary stream reads, but vectored I/O currently leaves large observability gaps.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  S3A input streams should publish dedicated vectored-read IO statistics so operators can understand how often vectored reads happen, how many ranges are requested, and how many bytes are discarded as part of those reads. The counters must use the public statistic names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges` so downstream tooling can consume them consistently.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Running vectored reads through S3A should update the new vectored IO counters alongside existing stream statistics. The statistics should be exposed through the standard IOStats surfaces with the exact metric names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges`.
16	
17	  '

title: HADOOP-18392. Propagate vectored s3a input stream stats to file system stats.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  S3A vectored reads now collect stream-level counters, but filesystem-level statistics still do not reflect that activity, leaving operators with an incomplete top-level view.


  ## Desired outcome

  Vectored-read statistics gathered by S3A input streams should be propagated up into filesystem statistics so monitoring at the filesystem layer sees the same workload patterns as stream-level diagnostics. This should enrich observability only; vectored read behavior itself must not change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running vectored reads through S3A should update both the input-stream counters and the aggregate filesystem statistics, including the vectored-read operation and range counters introduced for S3A. Existing vectored read success and error behavior should remain the same.

  '
title: HADOOP-18355. Update previous index properly while validating overlapping ranges.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Vectored-read callers rely on early validation to reject overlapping byte ranges, but a bookkeeping bug can leave the validator comparing the wrong prior range and miss a real overlap.


  ## Desired outcome

  `validateNonOverlappingAndReturnSortedRanges` should update its previous-range tracking correctly while it walks the sorted list, so any overlapping pair is rejected reliably. Callers should continue to get the same failure style they already expect for overlapping requests.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Overlapping ranges must still fail with `UnsupportedOperationException` carrying the message `Overlapping ranges are not supported`, and non-overlapping ranges should continue to be returned in sorted order. The fix should be in validation accuracy, not in changing the API surface.

  '
